properties.name: A what-if on a premise reaches what rests on it, not everything its parent requirement decomposes into, so two premises' reach can be told apart
properties.source: @ajs, 2026-10-19: "yes, I want them added to phase 6" (stage-5 re-read gaps)
properties.statement:
propagate_from (and propagate_change) seeded on a premise of a line of reasoning counts and lists what rests on that premise: the steps it is a premise of, their conclusions, and onward. A walk that climbs a DECOMPOSES edge to the parent requirement and fans back down to every sibling is reported apart from the reasoning reach (or not followed for a premise), so the totals and risk crossings of two different premises differ when their reach differs.
Observed in the stage-5 re-read (2026-10-19, flo2.io 7aa8a90d21c8956c, 0.88.0): what-ifs on Premise 2, Premise 5 and Premise 6, whose reasoning reach is 1, 4 and 1 steps, each reported total_impacted 66 and the same nine risk_crossings, because each premise DECOMPOSES the deliverable req:argument-is-the-deliverable and the walk fans out from there.
